Chocolate Letters

Served at: Sinterklaas Arrival (Intocht)

Makes 2-4 large chocolate letters (depending on mold size)Prep 20 min

Chocolate Letters, or 'chocoladeletters' in Dutch, are a beloved and iconic treat during the Sinterklaas season in the Netherlands. Traditionally, these solid chocolate letters are given to children and adults alike, often representing the first letter of their name, as part of the gift-giving festivities that follow Sinterklaas's arrival (Intocht). Making them at home allows for personalization and a truly special touch during this joyous time.

Ingredients

  • 16 ounces (450 g) good quality chocolate (milk, dark, or white, or a combination)
  • Optional: 1 teaspoon vanilla extract or other flavorings (e.g., orange zest, peppermint extract)
  • Optional: Sprinkles, chopped nuts, or small candies for decoration

Method

  1. Ensure your chocolate letter molds (silicone or plastic) are clean and completely dry. Moisture can cause chocolate to seize.
  2. Chop the chocolate into small, uniform pieces. This helps it melt evenly.
  3. Melt the chocolate using a double boiler method: Place about two-thirds of the chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (ensure the bottom of the bowl does not touch the water). Stir gently until melted and smooth.
  4. Alternatively, melt in a microwave: Heat the chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl in 30-second intervals, stirring well after each interval, until mostly melted. Remove from microwave and stir until completely smooth.
  5. Remove the melted chocolate from the heat (or microwave). Add the remaining one-third of chopped chocolate to the melted chocolate and stir continuously until it is fully melted and the mixture is smooth and glossy. This helps to 'temper' the chocolate slightly, giving it a better shine and snap without needing a full tempering process.
  6. If using, stir in any optional flavorings like vanilla extract at this stage.
  7. Carefully pour the melted chocolate into your prepared letter molds, filling them completely. If adding sprinkles or nuts, you can sprinkle them into the molds before or after pouring the chocolate, or press them onto the surface once poured.
  8. Gently tap the molds on your countertop a few times to release any trapped air bubbles. This ensures a smooth, solid letter.
  9. Place the filled molds in the refrigerator for at least 30-60 minutes, or until the chocolate is completely set and firm. Do not freeze.
  10. Once firm, carefully unmold the chocolate letters by gently flexing the silicone molds or pushing them out of rigid plastic molds. Handle them by the edges to avoid fingerprints.
  11. Store the chocolate letters in an airtight container at cool room temperature until ready to present for Sinterklaas.

Tips

  • For a truly professional finish with a great snap and shine, research proper chocolate tempering techniques. The 'seed method' used in step 5 is a simplified version.
  • Experiment with different types of chocolate within the same letter for a marbled effect, or use white chocolate and color it with oil-based food coloring.
  • To clean molds easily, wipe them with a paper towel after use; avoid washing with soap and water if possible, as residue can affect future chocolate batches.
